Text.Text: Look at you. The Hunger of the Dark, worn like a tailored coat. Our business is concluded, which is the only grief I permit myself. Feed well, stop while stopping is still a choice, and if you ever taste something down in the dark worth sharing, my table is always set.

You want something. Everyone who walks this far onto Korriban wants something, but you want the thing I keep, I can smell it. Come back when your grasp of the Force is a finished appetite, not a growing child's stomach. I do not waste good meals on the half-starved. They gorge, and they burst.

Stop. Do not tell me why you have come; let me have the pleasure. You want the hunger. The art of drawing the life out of a thing and pouring it into yourself, feeding without being eaten. Yes? Of course yes. And I want something too, which is how everything worth having begins. A coven squats in the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths below us, adepts gnawing on powers they cannot digest. Cull six of them and bring me the Hunger of the Dark Crypt Trial Tablet they slobber their prayers over. Do that, and I will start teaching you how to eat properly.

Sealed with appetite. Here is the key; it opens the stair down into the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths. Six adepts, one tablet, and back to me before anything else acquires a taste for you. And eat before you go. Fainting in a Sith crypt is such an undignified way to become dinner.

Anyone can devour. A rancor can devour. The discipline is in the digestion: taking a life's heat into yourself without letting its screaming become yours. The coven below never learned that. They gulp and gulp and wonder why they are always empty. I will teach you portion control, piece by piece, at my price. The tablet is the first installment.

Through the sealed stair into the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths. I hand you the key when we shake on it, so to speak. Down the stair, past the first tombs where nothing worth eating remains, into the rite-chambers. Follow the smell of overcooked ambition. The adepts never stray far from their tablet. Children cling to the cookbook.

Oh, they bite. Six of them, each one swollen on stolen vitae and starving anyway. They will try to drink you where you stand, and the delicious irony is that you are here to learn the very trick they will attempt. Watch how they do it wrong. That is the cheapest lesson on the menu, and it comes free.
Still six adepts on the menu, still one tablet with my name on it. Figuratively speaking. The crypt depths are patient. I am considerably less so.
There you are, and there it is. I can smell the crypt on the stone from here. Old hunger, badly seasoned. Hand the tablet over and we will call the first course served.

Nothing they miss matters anymore. Mm. Cruder than I hoped; the coven has been chewing the rite with their mouths open. Your payment, as agreed: credits, and the first lesson. You killed six feeders today and felt your own appetite watching them do it. Remember that feeling. We will be naming it soon.

Back for the second course. Good. The first was barely an appetizer. Deeper in, five specialists tend the coven's focus, the Hunger of the Dark Ritual Focus Shard. A pretty stone that holds everything they cannot keep down, all that stolen heat pooled where they can lap at it. Kill the five and bring the shard to me. I pay in teaching, which is the only currency of mine that appreciates.

Then it is agreed, and I already savor it. Down the stair, past your earlier leavings, and mind the pull when you get close. Carry the shard out quickly. Held too long, it starts making suggestions, and its suggestions are all recipes.

Badly? No. Precisely. That shard is a full pantry gathered by fools, years of swallowed life sitting in one stone because not one of them could digest it. In my hands it becomes curriculum. In yours, briefly, it becomes a lesson in carrying a feast you must not taste. Do not taste it. That is not one of my rules. It is a rule of anatomy.

Past the chambers you already emptied, where the galleries pinch tight and the air gets thick enough to chew. Five of them sit around the shard like diners who cannot leave the table. You will feel the pull before you see the light; the shard invites everyone. It invited them, once. Look how that ended.

Cooperate. The adepts fed alone; the specialists feed each other, passing your strength around their circle while you wonder why your knees have developed opinions. Break the circle and they are five hungry mouths. Leave it standing and you are the centerpiece. You see why I find teaching so easy? The syllabus keeps trying to eat the students.
The shard still sits in its circle of five. My pantry does not stock itself, and your next lesson is locked behind it. Go on. Work up an appetite.
Oh, I felt you coming this time. The shard sings through stone. And you did not taste it, did you? No. Look at you, still standing straight. Marvelous restraint. Hand it here.

It does that to everyone. Be flattered it thought you worth tempting. Payment in full: credits, and the second lesson. Hunger shared is hunger multiplied. That was their circle's whole trick, and you broke it. Keep that one. Further down, someone has built a much bigger table, and you are not yet ready to sit at it. Yet.

Now the meal turns serious. The breach into the deep tombs has a doorkeeper, the coven's warden, wearing the Hunger of the Dark Splintered Tomb Sigil like a bib. He has eaten everything sent down to move him, and I do mean everything; there are no bones. So take my honest advice, and note the novelty of me giving any: set a full table. Bring two companions whose strength you would happily borrow, because he will try to drink all three of you, and three is one more than he has ever managed.

Then it is a dinner engagement. Bring your two, keep them fed and standing, and remember: when he starts to drink from one of you, that is not the crisis. That is the opening. Carve while he swallows. Bring me the sigil with every splinter. I will count them.

Once, a rival of mine, if you can imagine anyone rivaling me. He went down to raid the coven's pantry and stayed to guard it, which tells you exactly what the deep tombs offer. Now he is appetite wearing armor, planted in the breach, fed by everything that tries to pass. He no longer wants to move. Wanting takes a self, and he traded his away for a fuller stomach.

Because feeding on a single target is his native art, my dear glutton-in-training. Alone, you are one cup, and he will drain you at his leisure between parries. Three vessels split his draw. While he sips one, two are cutting. It is arithmetic, not cowardice. I have watched him digest heroes who thought otherwise. They were very brave for almost a minute.

The seal of the deep tomb doors, splintered the night the coven forced them open to reach what was buried. Each splinter still remembers being whole, and things that remember wholeness are worth a fortune to a man in my line of study. Bring it up and I pay in the richest teaching yet. He will not part with it politely. Nothing he has swallowed has ever come back up.
The warden still bloats in the breach, and my sigil still decorates his chest. Do not go down light. Three at the table, or the table eats you.
You are back, and walking without assistance. So he is finally someone else's meal. The sigil, if you please. All the splinters.

All there, and still humming with old wholeness. Exquisite. You have done what a coven's worth of appetite could not, and you did it by sharing the meal. There is a lesson very few of my kind survive learning. Credits, and a truth for dessert: below the breach sits the inner circle, and below them, the one who swallowed too much. We are getting to the marrow now.

The inner circle. Four keepers who run the coven's kitchen, deciding who feeds and who is food. They hold the Hunger of the Dark Keeper's Rite Token, the little mark that makes their gluttony official. I want it. They are attached to it. You see the shape of the transaction. Starve the circle, all four, and pluck the token from whichever hand grips it last. After the warden, this is almost a light lunch. Almost.

Agreed and appetized. They can feel their coven thinning around them, the sigil gone, the shard silent, the pantry echoing. Frightened misers clutch hardest, so expect the token to cost all four deaths, exactly as promised. Bring it to me still warm. Metaphorically. Or not.

Restraint, of all things. The adepts gorge and the specialists pool, but the keepers ration. They keep the coven hungry on purpose, because hungry followers are obedient followers. It is nearly elegant, and it is entirely wasted on them. They hoard what they cannot digest and call the hoarding wisdom. A vault is not a stomach. Even they will learn that, briefly, when you arrive.

It is the coven's deed of table. Whoever bears it decides the portions: who feeds first, who feeds last, who is the feed. Take it and their whole hierarchy dies of hunger pangs. To me it is worth rather more, but that is between me and my studies, and my studies pay your tuition. Everyone eats. Is commerce not beautiful?

Keep your company if you enjoyed the warden's banquet; four keepers will happily restage it. They fight the way misers spend, grudging, careful, all together or not at all. Kill the generous one first. There is always one who spends strength too freely, and the other three lean on the habit. When the spendthrift falls, watch the rationing collapse.
Four keepers still ration the dark below, and my token still legitimizes them. Finish the circle. Nobody down there is getting any more tender.
And there it is. The coven's entire authority, small enough to swallow. They always are, in the end. Hand it over.

Perfect. The circle starves, the coven is a rumor, and the deed to their table changes hands. To mine, you will notice, which is where deeds belong. Your payment, plus the penultimate lesson: they hoarded, you spent, and spending won. Only the master remains, and he is the reason the words 'too much' exist. Rest. Sharpen. Come back famished.

The last course, and I will not dress it in sauce. At the bottom of everything sits the master, the appetite that founded the coven. He learned the true Hunger of the Dark, the very art you have been buying from me piece by piece, and then he kept feeding past the point where a self remains to be fed. There is nothing to bring me this time. His ending is the payment, and I will feel it through the stone the moment it happens. One warning, free of charge, because I have grown fond of my investment: no one leaves the master's table alone. Bring your two. He has emptied entire expeditions and called them a snack.

Then dinner is called. Down all three of you go, and mind the silence near the bottom. That is not peace. That is a cleaned plate. When he falls, do not linger over what spills out of him; some meals are cursed even by my standards. Come up, and come collect what I owe.

A cautionary text with a pulse. He mastered feeding without being eaten, truly mastered it, and then met the one predator no discipline stops: his own success. Every meal made the next one necessary. Now he is a hole shaped like a man, wielding our art perfectly and tasting none of it. Study him while you kill him. He is the final page of the book you are buying.

Honesty at last. I like it. His death vacates the deepest larder on Korriban and retires the only practitioner whose hunger outranks mine. And, I confess, I want to know it can be done. That the art has an ending other than becoming him. You are my experiment in eating well. Do give me a good result. I have wagered rather a lot of teaching on you.

Feed him confusion. Three vessels, always moving, never the same one in reach twice. His draw is bottomless but it is not quick, and greed makes him linger on whoever tastes strongest. Let your hardiest friend be the flavor, and open him up while he savors. And when the hunger in you leans toward him at the end, and it will lean, remember that you have somewhere to put your appetite. He is what forgetting that looks like.
The master still sits at the bottom, mid-meal as always. Three of you, no fewer, and nothing to carry back but the news. I am salivating on schedule.
I felt it an hour ago. The stone finally exhaled. The bottom of the crypt stands vacant, and the coven's whole line of gluttony dies with him. Say the words. I want to hear them said aloud.

Delicious. Then our contract completes: the Hunger of the Dark is yours, whole. The real art, feeding without being devoured, and you learned the part he never did, which is when to stop. Our account is settled, and that saddens me slightly. You were my favorite debt. Go. Be hungry out there in the wide galaxy. Just remember who taught you to chew.
Back to your bargain.
Done. Six adepts, one tablet. Then you teach.
What do you mean, eat properly?
How do I reach this coven?
What are these adepts capable of?
Your price needs thinking about.
One tablet. The adepts won't miss it.
About the shard again.
Five specialists, and the shard lands in your hands.
Why do you want the shard so badly?
Where do they keep it?
What can five do that six adepts couldn't?
Not hungry yet.
Take your pantry. It whispered the whole way up.
Back to the warden's table.
A full table, then. He can choke on the third course.
What exactly is this warden?
Why can't I take him alone?
And the sigil? What's it worth to you?
I need to find two more chairs first.
Count them. He didn't give them up gently.
Back to the keepers.
Four keepers. I'll bring you their table rights.
What makes the keepers different from the rest?
Why does the token matter?
Any advice for four at once?
Let them starve a little longer first.
The keepers are done rationing. Here's their token.
Back to the last course.
We'll all go down. He can try the whole table.
What did he become, exactly?
What do you get out of his death?
How do we survive his table?
Not until my companions are ready for it.
The master's table is closed. We ate; he didn't.
